hook_text: From space, parts of the Amazon look like a giant fishbone. What is eating the forest?
clip_script: A satellite photo of the Amazon in the 1970s: solid green. The same place years later: a long road with side roads branching off like the bones of a fish, and brown cleared land on both sides. Cattle ranches, soya farms, logging and mining have cleared the forest. Animals lose their homes, the thin soil washes away, rain changes and carbon goes into the air. But satellites, laws and protected areas can help.
visual_style: Whiteboard satellite view of green forest, then roads cutting in like a fishbone, with cattle, trucks of logs and a mine appearing, then patches of new green.
mood: Serious and concerned, ending with hope.
pacing: Slow before-and-after reveal, steady list of causes and effects, then a brighter close on solutions.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make a poster with three causes and three consequences of deforestation.
